title: Access Expiry Inspector and Workspace Settings — Audit-first Console Prototype
creator: Luca Chen
description:
Goal: Design an audit-first workspace settings and RBAC surface that helps security reviewers, workspace admins, and SREs quickly answer: who has access, why, when does that access expire, and which rollouts/changes impacted this state. The prototype focuses on two core flows: (1) Access Expiry Inspector: timeline view + compact row actions for bulk expiry and renewal; (2) Audit Trail Integrations inside Workspace Settings: filters, saved views, and links to cost/rollout context.

Scope and features in prototype:
- Timeline-first access view showing grants, role changes, and policy rollouts with delta highlights.
- Inline expiry badge and quick action menu (revoke, extend, request-approval) for each grant.
- Bulk selection mode with suggested remediation actions (auto-revoke expired, notify owners, create ticket).
- Saved audit filters (by role, by last-active, by expiry window, by rollout id).
- Cross-link: clicking a rollout entry opens the Rollouts panel with canary/test cohort and cost delta estimate.
- Lightweight RBAC editor: preview of effective permissions for a selected user or service account (no direct edit in prototype — edit surface is separate).
- Cost view integration: ability to filter cost breakdown by role-owner, helpful for cost accountability reviews.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first nav for timeline, clear focus ring for actions, color contrast verified against WCAG AA.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Timeline vs table: Timeline chosen for faster triage of recent changes and for surfacing rollouts as first-class events. Trade-off: less compact than a dense table for very large orgs. We included a compact-mode toggle for power users.
- Inline actions vs details panel: Inline quick actions for common tasks (revoke/extend/notify) to reduce click-through. Full context and reasoning live in the right-hand details panel to avoid accidental changes.
- Privacy vs audit transparency: We redact personally-identifiable fields in default view and provide an elevated audit mode for security reviewers. This requires an elevated permission check in the backend; marked as a dependency.

Prototype artifacts and links:
- Figma file (prototype v1): https://www.figma.com/file/RedwoodConsole/Access-Expiry-Inspector-V1
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CON/Access+Expiry+Inspector+Design+Spec
- GitHub PR (frontend prototype components): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4567
- Design QA checklist: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AuditQA_example

Acceptance criteria (for design handoff):
- Prototype annotated with interactions and accessibility notes.
- Edge-case flows documented: overlapping grants, service-account-only roles, expired-but-renewed events.
- Handoff tokens: color, spacing, iconography, component states, and example dataset for QA.
- API contract doc with required fields for audit event enrichment (event_type, actor_id, actor_type, grant_id, role_id, effective_permissions, expiry_ts, rollout_id).

Open questions for PM/Eng:
- Should 'elevated audit mode' be a workspace-level toggle or per-user permission? (PM leaning: per-user; Eng: pref workspace-level for simpler caching).
- How many events to show in timeline by default (50 vs 200)? Implication: backend pagination and cost.
- Cost linkage granularity: associate cost to "owner" of a role or to the specific rollout that created the change? Both have pros/cons for attribution.

Next steps and implementation plan:
- Iterate prototype based on design review feedback (due by 2025-02-22).
- Complete interaction spec and deliver Figma tokens to frontend (target 2025-02-25).
- Coordinate with ENG-3210 on elevated-audit API changes and cache invalidation.
- Run a short usability session with two security/review leads (schedule in Cycle 42).

Notes on related Console surfaces:
- Rollouts: prototype links to existing Rollouts panel; will require small extension to show cohort cost.
- Cost views: adds a new filter dimension 'role_owner' to existing cost breakdown.

Design assets included with ticket: static PNGs of timeline, compact table variant, details panel JSON dataset examples (attached in Confluence link above).
